sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 2.1 and footnote 3, p.4, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the passage is the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "Theorem 2.1. Let the notation be as above. Then we have ξ(h²_Q) = ξ((h¹/z)_Q), an equality of ideals in Z_p[[G_{p∞f}]]⊗Q." Footnote 3: "The formulation in Theorem 2.1 is then identical with the one in [11, §7.2]."
sourceIssues.correction: ξ((h¹/z)_Q) = ξ(h²_Q)·∏_{𝔩|f, 𝔩∤p} ξ(Z_p[[G_{p∞f}/D_𝔩]]_Q), D_𝔩 the decomposition group of 𝔩; equivalently ξ((h¹/z)_Q) = ξ(H²_Q) with H² = lim_{K'} H²(O_{K'}[1/pf], Z_p(1)), which is the module of Johnson-Leung–Kings §7.2. The printed equality holds when every prime factor of f lies above p, and after localizing at height-one primes on components ramified at every 𝔩|f with 𝔩∤p.
sourceIssues.reason: z is generated by the elliptic units of the single modulus p^n f (Kato §15.5), whose projection to a character χ carries ∏_{𝔩|f,𝔩∤p}(1 − χ(𝔩)Frob_𝔩^{−1}) (Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 7.7); JLK accordingly pair it with H² over O_K[1/pf]. BT's h² is the class-group limit, which Kato (15.6.2) identifies at height one with H² over O_K[1/p]. By purity, 0 → H²(O[1/p]) → H²(O[1/pf]) → ⊕_{𝔩|f,𝔩∤p} Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]] → 0, and since D_𝔩 has Z_p-rank one each term is torsion but not pseudo-null. On the trivial-character component 1 − Frob_𝔩^{−1} is a non-unit even after inverting p, so the printed equality fails whenever f has a prime factor not above p, and footnote 3's "identical" is false for h². The same imprecision is in Kato's quotation of Rubin (Astérisque 295, Theorem 15.2(2)); Rubin's elliptic units include all moduli g|f.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the passage is the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "In [12, §15] it is shown that the CM case of Kato's main conjecture [12, Conj. 12.10] in Λ⊗Q is a consequence of the equivariant main conjecture for the underlying imaginary quadratic field up to tensoring with Q."
sourceIssues.correction: Kato §15 deduces only the inequality length(H²(T~)_𝔭) ≤ length(H¹(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ,T)_𝔭) (Prop. 15.17) from Rubin's inequality. The equality needs a further step: apply Kato's Lemma 14.15 to both H²_q and H¹_q/A·z; the Ker(a|H²) terms of (15.13.1)–(15.13.2) cancel, and Ker(a|H¹_q/Az) = 0 because A is a regular local ring (a UFD), a is prime, H¹_q is torsion-free of rank one and z generates it at aA (Kato 15.15).
sourceIssues.reason: Kato lists Theorems 12.4–12.6, 14.2 and 14.5 as what §15 proves (p.250), not Conjecture 12.10. Prop. 15.17 (p.265) is an inequality, and on p.251 Kato writes that Rubin has an equality in some cases "but we do not use it in this paper". Nowhere in §15 is the equality stated. Checked on the page images of Astérisque 295.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, equation (3.1), p.6, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the passage is the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "Since H¹_f(Q,V_{Fλ}(f)(k/2)) = 0, by the exact sequence [12, (14.9.3)], note that (3.1) H²(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q = 0."
sourceIssues.correction: Apply (14.9.3) first to the Tate-dual lattice T(k/2)^*(1), a lattice in V(f*)(k/2) by (14.10.1): its Selmer term is controlled by the hypothesis, and with (14.9.5) and Prop. 14.12 this gives H¹_f(Q,V(f*)(k/2)) = 0. Then apply (14.9.3) to T(k/2).
sourceIssues.reason: A single application of (14.9.3) to T(k/2) involves the Selmer group of T(k/2)^*(1), which by (14.10.1) belongs to f*, not to the hypothesis. The two-step argument uses only statements in Kato §14; Kato's own p.242 remark uses the same device.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, choice of γ, p.6, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the passage is the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let ± = (−1)^{k/2−1} and pick γ ∈ V_{Fλ}(f) such that γ^± ≠ 0. … Hence Theorem 2.6 implies that z is an F_λ-basis of H¹(Z[1/p],T(k/2))⊗Q."
sourceIssues.correction: State and use Kato's sign relation z_{ι(γ)}(f) = −σ_{−1}z_γ(f) (Theorem 12.5(1)). It shows that at q the specialization of z_γ depends only on γ^±, and that the other component dies, so the image of the single class z_γ, not just of the module Z(f)_q, spans.
sourceIssues.reason: The main conjecture gives Z(f)_q = H¹_q, a statement about the module generated by all z_γ. Passing to one z_γ needs the sign relation, which the paper does not mention. The relation is printed in Kato Theorem 12.5(1) and derived on p.230.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 3.3 and its attribution, p.6, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the passage is the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "… due to Smith [21, Thm. 1.2]. Theorem 3.3. … for a density one subset of the square-free positive integers n ≡ 1,2,3 mod 8, corank_{Z_2}Sel_{2∞}(E^{(n)}/Q) = 0."
sourceIssues.correction: Theorem 3.3 is a consequence of Smith's Theorem 1.2, not its statement: pass from all nonzero integers to positive squarefree n, restrict to the classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8, and use the 2-parity theorem to exclude corank 1 there.
sourceIssues.reason: Smith's Theorem 1.2 (Part I, proved in Part II) orders all nonzero integers d with |d| ≤ H, both signs, and gives the proportions of 2∞-corank 0, 1 and ≥ 2. BT do not mention the parity step or the restriction. y² = x³ − x satisfies Smith's Assumption 1.1: it has full rational 2-torsion and no rational cyclic 4-isogeny. The extraction noted this (item smith-density).
